classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that adding a zero ordinate leaves the other ordinate unchanged.

inlines.text: Explain how they are quickly obtained.

spec.description: Black axes with positive-direction arrowheads and x and y labels; two unlabelled smooth component curves and seven supplied purple points. No grid, ticks, numerical scale or origin label.
spec.mathematics: The blue curve has one crest and one trough; the red curve has two crests separated by a trough. Each supplied purple point keeps the ordinate of one component at an x-intercept of the other. Drawing coordinates normalise the unscaled source sketch and do not specify equations or numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Both component curves and all seven supplied purple points remain visible in the question edition.

answer.short: At an $x$-intercept of either graph, its ordinate is zero, so the sum has the other graph's ordinate.
answer.worked: Each marked point has the same $x$-coordinate as an $x$-intercept of one graph. Add its zero ordinate to the other graph's ordinate; the other point is unchanged.
